title: How Fusion Energy Is Finally Becoming Real

slides.heading: Fusion Energy Is Finally Becoming Real
slides.body: After 70 years of research, limitless clean power is closer than ever

slides.heading: What Is Nuclear Fusion?
slides.body: Fusion is the process that powers the Sun — fusing hydrogen atoms together releases enormous energy. Unlike fission (splitting atoms), fusion produces no long-lived radioactive waste and is inherently safe.

slides.heading: The Old Joke: Always 30 Years Away
slides.body: For decades, fusion was called "the energy source of the future — and always will be." The challenge is sustaining a plasma hotter than the Sun's core (100 million°C) long enough to extract net energy.

slides.heading: The NIF Breakthrough
slides.body: In December 2022, the National Ignition Facility fired 2.05 MJ of laser energy at a tiny fuel pellet and got 3.15 MJ back — the first lab experiment to produce more fusion energy than the lasers delivered. The milestone was repeated and improved in 2023–2025.

slides.heading: Tokamaks: The Leading Design
slides.body: Most fusion reactors use a tokamak — a donut-shaped magnetic bottle that traps superhot plasma. ITER, the 35-nation megaproject in France, is expected to demonstrate 10× more power out than in by the early 2030s.

slides.heading: Private Companies Are Racing In
slides.body: Dozens of startups — Commonwealth Fusion Systems, TAE Technologies, Helion, and more — have raised billions of dollars. Helion has a power-purchase agreement with Microsoft and aims for commercial electricity by the late 2020s.

slides.heading: High-Temperature Superconductors Changed Everything
slides.body: New rare-earth barium copper oxide (REBCO) tapes can create magnetic fields of 20+ tesla at far lower cost. Commonwealth Fusion's compact SPARC tokamak uses these magnets to shrink a power plant to the size of a tennis court.

slides.heading: How Much Energy Could Fusion Provide?
slides.body: A single kilogram of fusion fuel (deuterium + tritium) yields energy equivalent to 10 million kilograms of coal. Deuterium is extracted from seawater — an essentially limitless supply for millions of years of civilization.

slides.heading: Remaining Challenges
slides.body: Tritium must be bred inside the reactor (it doesn't occur naturally in useful amounts). Materials that survive neutron bombardment for years are still being developed. Costs must fall dramatically to compete with solar and wind.

slides.heading: The Sun in a Bottle — Coming Soon?
slides.body: Fusion is no longer a distant dream. With record-breaking experiments, bold private investment, and new magnet technology, the 2030s may finally deliver commercial fusion power — clean, safe, and virtually limitless.
